name: Shoki Oda
notes: Fastest pitch recorded at Koshien (96.9 mph / 156 kph), hit seven times in one game. Velocity up every year. Reported to be weighing a direct MLB contract over the NPB draft.

name: Ryosuke Sueyoshi
reading: すえよし りょうすけ
notes: Won the national title as a second-year, then started the U-18 World Cup final. The most decorated résumé in the class. Thick lower half, late life on the fastball.

name: Haruki Komoda
notes: 6-foot-4 and 220 pounds at 18. Started all four games of a 2025 summer Koshien semifinal run and hits cleanup. Which side he plays in pro ball is an open question.

name: Taisei Suzuki
notes: Tohto League Most Valuable Pitcher. Moved from the bullpen to the rotation and is the highest-rated college arm in the class.

name: Kai Watabe
notes: Elite arm by any league's standard - MLB average pop time is around 2.00 s. Won a national title in high school at Chiben Wakayama, four straight Tohto titles in college, national team selection.

name: Kosei Hiroike
reading: ひろいけ こうせい
key_metric: 156 kph in the bullpen (~153 in games)
notes: Vice-captain at Keio. Father is a former NPB pitcher and currently a Seibu Lions front-office executive.

name: Kansuke Yoshioka
reading: よしおか かんすけ
notes: 5-foot-9 and throws 95 with high spin. Comparisons in Japan run to Kaima Taira. Small for the profile, which is the entire scouting question.

name: Shin Higuchi
key_metric: Best ERA in his rookie corporate season
notes: The top left-hander in the corporate ranks. Threw a nine-inning shutout in the 2025 Intercity Championship. Closest thing in this class to a finished product.

name: Hinata Fukushima
school_jp: 東海大学付属熊本星翔高校
notes: Arm strength measured off the mound at 146 kph. Hit .571 in the 2025 summer national tournament. The best up-the-middle athlete among the high schoolers.

name: Mahiro Sugimoto
notes: Strikeout left-hander who also plays the outfield. Carried Chiben Gakuen to the spring national final.

name: Ryo Tanaka
notes: Captain and catcher, 220 pounds. Hit .364 with two home runs in the 2025 summer national tournament as his team finished runner-up. Right-handed power in a low-bounce-bat era.

name: Gaku Arima
notes: Short left-hander with a two-seamer Japanese scouts call a trick pitch. The strikeout run at the national college tournament is the calling card.

name: Yuto Yonezawa
notes: Left-hander out of the Kansai Big Six. Compared domestically to Yuki Kanamaru.

name: Keigo Okada
notes: The fastest time recorded since Japan's college national team began using optical timing - faster than the Japanese track record for the distance. Leadoff second baseman.

name: Masato Shibazaki
notes: Rookie-of-the-year award in the corporate league. Plays all three outfield spots. Over 100 career hits at Osaka University of Economics.

name: Daito Furuki
notes: Captain at Ohtani's and Kikuchi's high school. Takes batting practice with a wood bat, which is unusual at this level in Japan. Father is a former NPB infielder.

name: Nanato Sakakibara
reading: さかきばら ななと
notes: Two-way player in high school who touched 145 kph; that arm now plays in center. Vice-captain at Meiji.

name: Akito Haruyama
key_metric: 10 league home runs; 3 HR in one game
notes: Right-handed power bat in the Kansai Big Six. The conference career home run record is 12.
